subject: Service offset proposal and invoice application after 2027-03-28 incident
messages:
From: Naoko Sato <naoko.sato@kyotoai.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: thomas.greene <thomas.greene@kyotoai.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: service offset calculation and invoice application after 3/28 latency incident

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the incident update you shared earlier. Our engineering team reviewed the postmortem and we see the degraded service window on 2027-03-28 between 02:17–02:44 UTC (approx 27 minutes) impacted several production routes. We need two things from Redwood to close our procurement/finance loop:

1) Confirmation of SLA eligibility and the method you'll use to calculate the service offset (minutes, percent, proration).
2) A proposal for how that credit will be applied — ideally as a one-time credit on our April invoice (invoice number PO-99214 attached).

We're trying to reconcile this quickly because Q2 close is next week. I attached our internal incident summary and the PO. If you could provide the calculation and a draft credit memo we can route to finance, that would be great.

Best,
Naoko Sato
Head of Platform, KyotoAI
naoko.sato@kyotoai.com
Attachments: incident_summary_20270328.pdf, PO-99214.pdf
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Naoko Sato <naoko.sato@kyotoai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: service offset calculation and invoice application after 3/28 latency incident

Hi Naoko —

Thanks for the note and for attaching the PO. We can confirm we received your incident summary. Based on our initial review the 27-minute window is within the scope of the SLA clause for availability-based offsets. I'll loop in Marcus from Ops for the exact proration math and Laura in finance to confirm crediting mechanics (invoice vs. account credit).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marcus will run the eligibility calculation and share the raw numbers (downtime minutes, effective outage percent, capped credit).
- If eligible, we will prepare a credit memo/draft and propose applying it to your April invoice (per your ask).

I'll have a preliminary calc back to you by end of day.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachment: prelim_credit_calc_olga.xlsx (internal)
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Naoko Sato <naoko.sato@kyotoai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: service offset calculation and invoice application after 3/28 latency incident

Hi all —

I ran the eligibility calc using the standard SLO in your contract (99.9% monthly availability, credits tiered per Appendix A). Method used:
- Window observed: 2027-03-28 02:17–02:44 UTC = 27 minutes outage/degradation for affected routes.
- Monthly window for March: 31 days = 44,640 minutes.
- Outage percent = 27 / 44,640 = 0.0605% reduction in availability.

Per Appendix A:
- <0.1% reduction => 10% service credit on monthly service fees for affected routes;
- Credits are capped at 50% monthly fee and applied pro rata to affected service lines.

KyotoAI usage breakdown for March (from billing):
- gen.small and gen.large routing accounted for 72% of your bill; embeddings 18%; other 10%.
- Estimated monthly bill (March): $48,200 (reviewed against billing system).

Preliminary calculation (conservative):
- Base monthly fee portion affected: $48,200 * 0.72 = $34,704
- 10% credit on affected portion = $3,470.40
- Apply proration for partial month impact? Incident in March — we will apply as credit on March billing cycle but per your request can apply to April invoice.

Notes & controls:
- We honor contract Appendix A; if you prefer we can provide token-level logs to justify route-level allocation.
- I attached the runbook that shows calc steps and a spreadsheet (Olga's prelim file) that I used to arrive at the numbers.

If accepted, Laura (finance) will create a credit memo for $3,470.40 and we can post it against April invoice.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Operational Reliability (Redwood Inference)
Attachments: slo_runbook_v2.pdf
From: Naoko Sato <naoko.sato@kyotoai.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: thomas.greene <thomas.greene@kyotoai.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: service offset calculation and invoice application after 3/28 latency incident

Thanks Marcus — that methodology looks reasonable. Two quick clarifications:
1) Can you confirm whether the $3,470.40 will be issued as a one-time credit memo applied to the April invoice (preferred) or as an account credit that carries forward? We prefer invoice-level credits for our audit trail.
2) Please confirm the credit memo will reference PO-99214 and our vendor code KYT-4437 so our procurement team can match it.

Once you confirm we will sign off and Thomas will follow up on any additional documentation for procurement.

Best,
Naoko
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Request: service offset calculation and invoice application after 3/28 latency incident

Hi Naoko —

Thanks everyone. KyotoAI confirmed PO-99214 and vendor code KYT-4437. Finance will issue credit memo CM-2027-0410 for $3,470.40 and apply it to your April 30 invoice. Expected posting date: 2027-04-10.

Summary for your records:
- Incident: 2027-03-28 02:17–02:44 UTC (27m)
- Calculation method: Appendix A (99.9% SLA), 10% credit on affected service portion
- Calculated credit: $3,470.40
- Credit memo: CM-2027-0410 (to be posted 2027-04-10)
- Applied to: April 30, 2027 invoice (notes: references PO-99214, KYT-4437)

I'll close the loop here once the credit posts and share a confirmation receipt. Apologies again for the impact — we're following up on remediation items to reduce recurrence.

—Olga
